neighbours.label: residents, homes and businesses as the people affected by a local hazard (nearby residents told to stay indoors, homes and businesses flooded)
fire: Health officials told nearby residents to stay indoors until the smoke cleared.
The storm surge flooded homes and businesses along the waterfront.
After the gas leak, police urged local residents to leave their houses.
The wildfire forced hundreds of families to abandon their ranches overnight.
Toxic algae blooms angered residents and business owners along the coast.
Officials advised people living near the plant not to drink well water.
The power outage left thousands of homes and businesses without heat.
A boil-water notice was issued to residents of the eastern suburbs.
quiet: Health officials said the smoke had cleared by the afternoon.
The storm surge washed sand across the coastal highway.
After the gas leak, crews repaired the pipe under the street.
The wildfire burned through dry grass on the empty hillside overnight.
Toxic algae blooms turned the coastal water a murky green.
Officials said the plant had passed its safety inspection.
The power outage was caused by a fallen tree on the main line.
A new water main was installed under the eastern suburbs.
